pathway.title: HERC HOLDINGS INC — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: First, the issuer's leverage is falling because of earnings, not repayment. Gross debt moved from USD 8,103 million at FY2025 to USD 8,080 million at Q3 2026 while LTM reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,497 million to USD 1,932 million, taking gross debt to EBITDA from 5.41x to 4.18x and net debt to EBITDA from 5.38x to 4.15x [CP-1 leverage chart]. Mechanism: the acquisition debt was carried in full against earnings that only became a full-year contribution in the LTM to Q3 2026, so the earlier ratios were inflated by the part-year earnings base and the later ratio is the first clean one. Implication: further deleveraging has to come from continued EBITDA growth or from using free cash flow to repay debt, and the filings show gross debt essentially flat so far (Analyst Interpretation).

Second, fleet reinvestment absorbs much of the earnings that leverage ratios count. Net rental equipment spending was USD 857 million over the LTM, leaving USD 1,075 million of EBITDA after fleet reinvestment, so gross debt is 7.52x that residual [CP-1 calculations]. Mechanism: rental depreciation is added back in EBITDA while the fleet must be replaced in cash. Implication: the credit's repayment capacity is set by the spread between EBITDA and fleet spending, and the raised outlook for net rental capex of USD 1,000 million to USD 1,100 million for FY2026 against USD 737 million spent in 9M 2026 implies USD 263 million to USD 363 million more in Q4 2026 (Documentary Fact for the figures, Management Language for the outlook).

Third, liquidity is adequate but concentrated. Cash was USD 66 million and ABL availability under the borrowing base was USD 2,034 million at Q3 2026, for USD 2,100 million, up from USD 1,932 million at FY2025; the AR Facility is fully drawn at USD 550 million and matures on August 31, 2027, within twelve months of the balance sheet date [CP-1 liquidity chart]. Mechanism: the revolver is the buffer for seasonal swings and for unpaid fleet purchases of USD 252 million. Implication: a borrowing-base shortfall would cut liquidity even without any covenant breach, because the only financial maintenance test is a springing fixed charge ratio of 1.00:1.00 whose trigger is not quantified.

Fourth, interest is a heavy fixed charge. Cash interest paid over the LTM was USD 530 million against EBITDA of USD 1,932 million, giving 3.65x cover; Senior Notes coupons add up to USD 318.75 million a year and floating debt of USD 3,244 million is 40.1% of gross debt [CP-1 calculations]. Mechanism: coupon dates make single quarters lumpy, with cash interest of USD 169 million in Q2 2026 and USD 81 million in Q3 2026. Implication: trailing measures are the reliable ones, and short-term rates feed directly into a large share of the debt.

Fifth, the business context lowers cyclical risk without removing it. National accounts were 49% of FY2025 equipment rental revenue and no customer exceeded 3%, but demand is construction-linked, seasonal and, per management, project-led [CP-1A company and operating model]. Management's own net leverage of 3.90x uses pro forma adjusted EBITDA that cannot be rebuilt from the pack, and the synergy plan has no stated amount; both are Management Language and are not adopted.

runs.text: Strengths. Demand is diversified and project-supported (Documentary Fact): contractors, industrial, infrastructure and government, commercial facilities and other customers all contribute, national accounts were 49% of FY2025 equipment rental revenue and no customer exceeded 3% [CP-1A company and operating model]; this supports revenue visibility and bounds single-name loss. Liquidity is sound (Documentary Fact): USD 2,100 million at Q3 2026 with no financial maintenance covenant active and the company stating compliance [CP-1 liquidity and covenants]; this supports seasonal and capex funding without capital-market access. The nearest Senior Notes maturity is 2029 (Documentary Fact): the December 2025 refinancing redeemed the 2027 notes at par, so the 2026 to 2028 maturities in the year-end schedule are USD 26 million, USD 21 million and USD 497 million [CP-1 maturity chart; CP-1A transaction summary]; this limits refinancing pressure on the unsecured stack until 2029, subject to the AR Facility (USD 550 million, due August 31, 2027) and the ABL (due June 2, 2030). Earnings are rising (Documentary Fact): LTM reported EBITDA of USD 1,932 million against USD 1,497 million at FY2025 and a Q3 2026 dollar utilization of 43.5% (a management operating measure) [CP-1; CP-1A operating model]; this supports debt service. Capital allocation conduct is neutral to supportive (Analyst Interpretation): no repurchases in FY2025, Cinelease proceeds applied to debt and the 2027 notes refinanced at par [CP-1A governance behaviour]; this limits leakage, although the dividend continued at USD 0.70 per share each quarter.

Weaknesses. Leverage is high (Documentary Fact for the ratios, which are CP-1 calculations on unadjusted EBITDA): 4.18x gross and 4.15x net at Q3 2026 and USD 8,080 million of gross debt [CP-1]; this leaves limited tolerance for a downturn. Fleet capital intensity is heavy (Documentary Fact): EBITDA after net rental capex of USD 1,075 million, 7.52x gross debt, and negative Q3 2026 free cash flow of USD 69 million with USD 252 million of fleet purchases unpaid [CP-1]; this slows repayment and increases revolver use. Liquidity depends on one facility (Documentary Fact): ABL availability of USD 2,034 million is borrowing-base dependent and the AR Facility is fully drawn [CP-1]. Interest burden and floating-rate exposure (Documentary Fact): cash interest of USD 530 million over the LTM, cover of 3.65x and floating debt of USD 3,244 million [CP-1]; this exposes cash flow to short-term rates and the company says it is reevaluating its approach to floating-rate debt [CP-1A operating model], but no hedging program is described. Balance sheet quality (Documentary Fact): goodwill and intangible assets exceed equity, leaving tangible equity of negative USD 2,434 million [CP-1]; asset coverage rests on the fleet rather than on book equity. Structural position of the unsecured notes (Analyst Interpretation): USD 4,750 million of Senior Notes are unsecured and effectively junior to the secured ABL, term loan and AR Facility (USD 3,244 million drawn) to the extent of the value of collateral, and the ABL permits future pari passu or subordinated secured debt [CP-1 debt by instrument; CP-1A transaction summary]; no priming action is documented. Unverified management claims (Management Language): synergies tracking to plan and the 3.90x pro forma leverage, neither testable from the pack.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: H&E Equipment Services, Inc. acquisition (Documentary Fact, completed). On June 2, 2025 Herc Holdings completed the acquisition of all outstanding H&E common stock under a merger agreement dated February 19, 2025, paying "$78.75 in cash and 0.1287 shares of Company common stock on a per-H&E share basis" for a total purchase price of 4.8 billion US dollars, made up of 2.9 billion in cash and about 4.7 million Herc shares valued at 584m, with a further 1.4 billion of H&E debt repaid in cash and not assumed (Q3 10-Q page:15; 10-K page:97). There is no sponsor and no seller other than H&E's public shareholders. H&E brought approximately 160 branches in over 30 states and 2,500 team members (10-K page:8, page:97). Management calls it "the largest in the history of our industry" (Q1 release page:1; Management Language, not adopted). Funding was new debt: 2.8 billion in senior unsecured notes (the 7.00% Senior Notes due 2030 at 1.65 billion and the 7.25% Senior Notes due 2033 at 1.1 billion), a 750m Term Loan Facility and 2.5 billion of borrowings under a new ABL Credit Facility, of which approximately 1.6 billion repaid the prior ABL (10-K page:97, page:57). A senior secured 364-day bridge facility of up to 4.5 billion was committed in February 2025, undrawn, and terminated after the notes, term loan and ABL were in place (10-K page:118). Transaction expenses tied to H&E were 193m in FY2025, including a 64m termination fee paid on H&E's behalf, 27m of advisory fees and 21m of bridge commitment fees (10-K page:98). The purchase price allocation recorded customer relationships of 1,190 with a ten-year life and goodwill of 2,171 after a 12m measurement-period reduction in Q2 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:15-16); the 10-K showed goodwill of 2,183 before that adjustment (logged under Conflicts). Liquidity and leverage effect: total debt as printed rose from 4,086 at December 31, 2024 to 8,047 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:103); CP-1 gross debt was 8,103 at FY2025 and 8,080 at Q3 2026 (Analyst Interpretation: the acquisition debt is carried in full against earnings that became a full-year contribution only in the LTM to Q3 2026). Integration status is Management Language: Q1 release page:1 states the company "successfully completed the integration of our H&E acquisition" and Q3 10-Q page:25 states "We have completed the integration of H&E and continue to focus on realizing the anticipated operational synergies". The synergy plan is described as running "over our three-year synergy plan" (Q1 release page:1) without a stated amount; this is Insufficient Information and is a gap, not an adverse finding.

New debt issues (Documentary Fact). On June 2, 2025 the 7.00% Senior Notes due 2030 (1.65 billion) and 7.25% Senior Notes due 2033 (1.1 billion) were issued, with the Term Loan Facility (750m, SOFR plus 1.75% after a December 2025 repricing amendment) and the new ABL (maximum 4.0 billion; matures June 2, 2030). On December 16, 2025 the company issued 600m of 5.75% Senior Notes due 2031 and 600m of 6.00% Senior Notes due 2034 and, with other borrowings, redeemed the 1.2 billion 5.50% Senior Notes due 2027 at 100.00% of principal, recording a 2m loss on extinguishment (10-K page:104, page:108, page:112). The June 7, 2024 6.625% Senior Notes due 2029 (800m) remain outstanding. Mechanism and implication: the December refinancing removed the nearest unsecured maturity and moved the next notes maturity to 2029, so the near-dated debt is the AR Facility and the revolver rather than the notes; CP-1 shows the debt maturing schedule at December 31, 2025. All notes are senior unsecured, guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries, with a change of control repurchase offer at 101% (10-K page:105); the filings describe the ABL as permitting "future secured debt on a basis either pari passu with, or subordinated to, the liens securing the New ABL Credit Facility" (10-K page:114), which is legal capacity that could dilute the unsecured notes' asset coverage; no such issuance is documented.

Other 2025 and 2026 events (Documentary Fact). Otay Mesa Sales was acquired on July 16, 2024 for about 273m using cash and ABL drawings (10-K page:98). Cinelease was sold on July 31, 2025 for initial cash consideration of 100m plus earnouts, after a 49m pre-tax loss on assets held for sale in Q2 2025, and "the net proceeds from the sale of Cinelease" were used "to repay indebtedness" (10-K page:57, page:101); an earnout receivable of 32m is carried at fair value and depends on Cinelease revenue in 2027 and 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:22). The AR Facility was extended in August 2025 and increased from 400m to 475m in December 2025, to 500m in May 2026, and in August 2026 to 550m with maturity extended to August 31, 2027 (10-K page:57; Q3 10-Q page:18). In July 2026 the company replaced certain insurance-related bank letters of credit with surety-backed letters of credit, adding about 25m of ABL capacity (Q3 10-Q page:32). Subsequent event after the Q3 period end: on October 27, 2026 the company raised its FY2026 outlook (Q3 release page:4); no other post-quarter event is stated in the sources.

fields.value: Two limits shape how far the ratios can be pushed. First, the only EBITDA that can be built for every window is the company's unadjusted EBITDA (net income plus tax, net interest, rental depreciation and non-rental depreciation and amortization). Adjusted EBITDA is printed for the 2026 quarters, 6M and 9M and their 2025 comparatives, but not for FY2025 or Q4 2025, so no trailing adjusted EBITDA exists in the pack. Second, the H&E acquisition closed on June 2, 2025, so the LTM windows to FY2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 contain months before the acquired earnings arrive while the year-end debt already funds them; their leverage is overstated against a pro forma view, and only the LTM to Q3 2026 (October 2025 to September 2026) is a clean post-acquisition window. Management's net leverage of 3.90x at Q3 2026 uses pro forma trailing adjusted EBITDA and is shown as attributed management data only. A ratio calculated here is a CP-1 calculation, not a covenant or management figure.

fields.value: No financial maintenance covenants apply to the ABL Credit Facility, AR Facility, Term Loan Facility or Notes. Under the ABL, "failure to maintain certain levels of liquidity" triggers a fixed charge coverage ratio of not less than 1:1 for the four most recent quarters; at September 30, 2026 "the appropriate levels of liquidity have been maintained", so the test is not applicable and the company states it was in compliance with all applicable covenants (Q3 10-Q page:33; 10-K page:115). The trigger level of liquidity or excess availability and the covenant's own definition of fixed charge coverage are not quantified in the filings, so headroom is Not calculable. The covenant definition would differ from the EBITDA used here: the ABL ratio is a fixed charge ratio on the credit agreement's own definitions, not EBITDA over cash interest. The indentures contain incurrence-type limitations on debt, restricted payments and liens, and a change of control put at 101% (10-K page:105), described at summary level only. Dividends are restricted by the debt agreements (Q3 10-Q page:33).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Leverage fell mainly because earnings grew, not because debt was repaid.** Gross debt moved from 8,103 at FY2025 to 8,080 at Q3 2026 (calc), while LTM unadjusted EBITDA rose from 1,497 to 1,932 (calc) as the H&E contribution replaced pre-acquisition months in the window and the 2026 quarters grew. The mechanism is the acquisition debt carried in full against a part-year earnings base at year-end; the credit implication is that deleveraging depends on EBITDA delivery and fleet-spending discipline rather than on scheduled amortization (the term loan amortizes at 1.00% a year). The LTM to Q3 2026 window starts after the H&E closing, so the stated pro forma element should add little there. Analyst interpretation: management's lower 3.90x is therefore mostly add-backs rather than pro forma earnings; this cannot be verified without FY2025 adjusted EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Fleet reinvestment absorbs much of the EBITDA.** Net rental equipment capex was 857 over the LTM (calc) and the raised outlook of US$1,000m to US$1,100m for FY2026 against 737 in 9M 2026 implies Q4 2026 net rental capex of 263 to 363 (calc). Operating cash flow of 951 in 9M 2026 exceeded net capex and left company-defined free cash flow of 133, but derived free cash flow was negative in Q3 2026 and equipment purchases in payables rose to 252 from 19 at FY2025 (10-K page:81; Q3 10-Q page:6). The implication is that liquidity must absorb timing swings in fleet payments, and the revolver, not internally generated cash, is the buffer.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Interest is mostly fixed and lumpy by coupon dates.** The five Senior Notes (4,750, fixed rate) carry coupons that sum to 318.75 a year (calc), paid on June 15 and December 15 for the 2029, 2030 and 2033 Notes and on March 15 and September 15 for the 2031 and 2034 Notes. That explains cash interest of 169 in Q2 2026 against 81 in Q3 2026 (calc). Floating debt (ABL, Term Loan, AR Facility) is 3,244 at September 30, 2026, which is 40.1% of gross debt (calc), so a change in short-term rates feeds directly into that share. Weighted stated rates at September 30, 2026 were 5.24% (ABL), 5.64% (Term Loan) and 4.49% (AR Facility) against 5.10%, 5.52% and 4.68% at December 31, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:17; 10-K page:103), so floating costs were not lower than at year-end. Indicative annual interest at September 30, 2026 stated rates is 491.65 (calc), against LTM cash interest of 530 and Q3 2026 interest expense of 126, which brackets a run-rate near 500.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Liquidity depends on the borrowing base and a single facility.** Cash plus ABL availability was 2,100 at Q3 2026, up from 1,932 at FY2025, helped by lower ABL borrowings and the replacement of 25 of bank letters of credit with surety-backed ones. The AR Facility is fully drawn and matures August 31, 2027; the company classifies it as long-term on its intent and ability to refinance it or use ABL capacity (Q3 10-Q page:18), which makes the revolver the fallback. The ABL matures June 2, 2030. No maintenance covenant restricts drawing, but a fixed charge test would apply if availability fell below an unquantified level.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: **Balance sheet quality.** Goodwill of 2,859 and intangible assets of 1,559 exceed total equity of 1,984, so tangible equity is negative 2,434 (calc). Rental equipment, net was 6,190 against secured debt of 3,244 (ABL, Term Loan, AR Facility; ratio 1.91x, calc), but the rental equipment is also the main collateral for the ABL and Term Loan, so the unsecured Notes of 4,750 rank behind those claims on the same assets.

fields.value: The credit story is a scaled, fragmented-market equipment renter that doubled its footprint in one transaction and is now working through the leverage that transaction created. Operating facts are well documented and issuer-specific: one reportable segment, a fleet with original equipment cost of about US$10.0 billion at Q3 2026, 615 locations, a diversified end-market mix with national accounts at 49% of FY2025 rental revenue, and demand that management ties to large projects. The transaction facts are also well documented: the H&E acquisition, its funding mix, the December 2025 refinancing of the 2027 notes, the Cinelease sale and the 2026 AR Facility upsizing. Ownership is the thinnest area: the filings identify no sponsor, parent or controlling holder, but the holder detail sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied, so control and alignment are Insufficient Information rather than a conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The mechanisms that matter to a creditor are these. Rental revenue is earned on a fleet that must be continually replaced, so cash conversion is set by the gap between EBITDA and fleet spending, not by EBITDA alone (CP-1 shows EBITDA after net rental capex of US$1,075m on LTM EBITDA of US$1,932m). The acquisition was paid for mostly with new secured and unsecured debt, and the unsecured Senior Notes rank behind secured facilities that can reach a maximum of US$4,000m under the ABL plus the US$750m term loan, so the pool of assets that cover the notes depends on how much of the ABL is drawn. Management states the integration is complete and that revenue and cost synergies "are tracking to plan" (Q2 release page:1), but no synergy target or bridge is supplied, so the earnings uplift that deleveraging needs cannot be tested from the filings. Cyclical and seasonal demand, fuel and delivery cost inflation, and floating-rate exposure are the stated operating pressures.

fields.value: H&E Equipment Services, Inc. acquisition (Documentary Fact, completed). On June 2, 2025 Herc Holdings completed the acquisition of all outstanding H&E common stock under a merger agreement dated February 19, 2025, paying "$78.75 in cash and 0.1287 shares of Company common stock on a per-H&E share basis" for a total purchase price of 4.8 billion US dollars, made up of 2.9 billion in cash and about 4.7 million Herc shares valued at 584m, with a further 1.4 billion of H&E debt repaid in cash and not assumed (Q3 10-Q page:15; 10-K page:97). There is no sponsor and no seller other than H&E's public shareholders. H&E brought approximately 160 branches in over 30 states and 2,500 team members (10-K page:8, page:97). Management calls it "the largest in the history of our industry" (Q1 release page:1; Management Language, not adopted). Funding was new debt: 2.8 billion in senior unsecured notes (the 7.00% Senior Notes due 2030 at 1.65 billion and the 7.25% Senior Notes due 2033 at 1.1 billion), a 750m Term Loan Facility and 2.5 billion of borrowings under a new ABL Credit Facility, of which approximately 1.6 billion repaid the prior ABL (10-K page:97, page:57). A senior secured 364-day bridge facility of up to 4.5 billion was committed in February 2025, undrawn, and terminated after the notes, term loan and ABL were in place (10-K page:118). Transaction expenses tied to H&E were 193m in FY2025, including a 64m termination fee paid on H&E's behalf, 27m of advisory fees and 21m of bridge commitment fees (10-K page:98). The purchase price allocation recorded customer relationships of 1,190 with a ten-year life and goodwill of 2,171 after a 12m measurement-period reduction in Q2 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:15-16); the 10-K showed goodwill of 2,183 before that adjustment (logged under Conflicts). Liquidity and leverage effect: total debt as printed rose from 4,086 at December 31, 2024 to 8,047 at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:103); CP-1 gross debt was 8,103 at FY2025 and 8,080 at Q3 2026 (Analyst Interpretation: the acquisition debt is carried in full against earnings that became a full-year contribution only in the LTM to Q3 2026). fields.value: New debt issues (Documentary Fact). On June 2, 2025 the 7.00% Senior Notes due 2030 (1.65 billion) and 7.25% Senior Notes due 2033 (1.1 billion) were issued, with the Term Loan Facility (750m, SOFR plus 1.75% after a December 2025 repricing amendment) and the new ABL (maximum 4.0 billion; matures June 2, 2030). On December 16, 2025 the company issued 600m of 5.75% Senior Notes due 2031 and 600m of 6.00% Senior Notes due 2034 and, with other borrowings, redeemed the 1.2 billion 5.50% Senior Notes due 2027 at 100.00% of principal, recording a 2m loss on extinguishment (10-K page:104, page:108, page:112). The June 7, 2024 6.625% Senior Notes due 2029 (800m) remain outstanding. Mechanism and implication: the December refinancing removed the nearest unsecured maturity and moved the next notes maturity to 2029, so the near-dated debt is the AR Facility and the revolver rather than the notes; CP-1 shows the debt maturing schedule at December 31, 2025. All notes are senior unsecured, guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries, with a change of control repurchase offer at 101% (10-K page:105); the filings describe the ABL as permitting "future secured debt on a basis either pari passu with, or subordinated to, the liens securing the New ABL Credit Facility" (10-K page:114), which is legal capacity that could dilute the unsecured notes' asset coverage; no such issuance is documented.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Herc Holdings is a large, well-diversified equipment renter with an adequate but thin credit profile: it is highly levered after paying for H&E mostly with debt. Its strongest support is demand spread across end markets, with national accounts at 49% of FY2025 rental revenue, no customer above 3%, USD 2,100 million of liquidity, no maintenance covenants and no Senior Notes maturing before 2029. Its weakest point is cash conversion: gross debt of USD 8,080 million is 4.18x LTM reported EBITDA but 7.52x EBITDA after net rental capex, and free cash flow turned negative in Q3 2026. What decides the outcome is whether earnings growth and synergies reduce leverage faster than fleet spending, rates and fuel costs absorb it, with the ABL borrowing base as the buffer [CP-1, CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, the issuer's leverage is falling because of earnings, not repayment. Gross debt moved from USD 8,103 million at FY2025 to USD 8,080 million at Q3 2026 while LTM reported EBITDA rose from USD 1,497 million to USD 1,932 million, taking gross debt to EBITDA from 5.41x to 4.18x and net debt to EBITDA from 5.38x to 4.15x [CP-1 leverage chart]. Mechanism: the acquisition debt was carried in full against earnings that only became a full-year contribution in the LTM to Q3 2026, so the earlier ratios were inflated by the part-year earnings base and the later ratio is the first clean one. Implication: further deleveraging has to come from continued EBITDA growth or from using free cash flow to repay debt, and the filings show gross debt essentially flat so far (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, fleet reinvestment absorbs much of the earnings that leverage ratios count. Net rental equipment spending was USD 857 million over the LTM, leaving USD 1,075 million of EBITDA after fleet reinvestment, so gross debt is 7.52x that residual [CP-1 calculations]. Mechanism: rental depreciation is added back in EBITDA while the fleet must be replaced in cash. Implication: the credit's repayment capacity is set by the spread between EBITDA and fleet spending, and the raised outlook for net rental capex of USD 1,000 million to USD 1,100 million for FY2026 against USD 737 million spent in 9M 2026 implies USD 263 million to USD 363 million more in Q4 2026 (Documentary Fact for the figures, Management Language for the outlook).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, liquidity is adequate but concentrated. Cash was USD 66 million and ABL availability under the borrowing base was USD 2,034 million at Q3 2026, for USD 2,100 million, up from USD 1,932 million at FY2025; the AR Facility is fully drawn at USD 550 million and matures on August 31, 2027, within twelve months of the balance sheet date [CP-1 liquidity chart]. Mechanism: the revolver is the buffer for seasonal swings and for unpaid fleet purchases of USD 252 million. Implication: a borrowing-base shortfall would cut liquidity even without any covenant breach, because the only financial maintenance test is a springing fixed charge ratio of 1.00:1.00 whose trigger is not quantified.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, interest is a heavy fixed charge. Cash interest paid over the LTM was USD 530 million against EBITDA of USD 1,932 million, giving 3.65x cover; Senior Notes coupons add up to USD 318.75 million a year and floating debt of USD 3,244 million is 40.1% of gross debt [CP-1 calculations]. Mechanism: coupon dates make single quarters lumpy, with cash interest of USD 169 million in Q2 2026 and USD 81 million in Q3 2026. Implication: trailing measures are the reliable ones, and short-term rates feed directly into a large share of the debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, the business context lowers cyclical risk without removing it. National accounts were 49% of FY2025 equipment rental revenue and no customer exceeded 3%, but demand is construction-linked, seasonal and, per management, project-led [CP-1A company and operating model]. Management's own net leverage of 3.90x uses pro forma adjusted EBITDA that cannot be rebuilt from the pack, and the synergy plan has no stated amount; both are Management Language and are not adopted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Demand is diversified and project-supported (Documentary Fact): contractors, industrial, infrastructure and government, commercial facilities and other customers all contribute, national accounts were 49% of FY2025 equipment rental revenue and no customer exceeded 3% [CP-1A company and operating model]; this supports revenue visibility and bounds single-name loss. Liquidity is sound (Documentary Fact): USD 2,100 million at Q3 2026 with no financial maintenance covenant active and the company stating compliance [CP-1 liquidity and covenants]; this supports seasonal and capex funding without capital-market access. The nearest Senior Notes maturity is 2029 (Documentary Fact): the December 2025 refinancing redeemed the 2027 notes at par, so the 2026 to 2028 maturities in the year-end schedule are USD 26 million, USD 21 million and USD 497 million [CP-1 maturity chart; CP-1A transaction summary]; this limits refinancing pressure on the unsecured stack until 2029, subject to the AR Facility (USD 550 million, due August 31, 2027) and the ABL (due June 2, 2030). Earnings are rising (Documentary Fact): LTM reported EBITDA of USD 1,932 million against USD 1,497 million at FY2025 and a Q3 2026 dollar utilization of 43.5% (a management operating measure) [CP-1; CP-1A operating model]; this supports debt service. Capital allocation conduct is neutral to supportive (Analyst Interpretation): no repurchases in FY2025, Cinelease proceeds applied to debt and the 2027 notes refinanced at par [CP-1A governance behaviour]; this limits leakage, although the dividend continued at USD 0.70 per share each quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage is high (Documentary Fact for the ratios, which are CP-1 calculations on unadjusted EBITDA): 4.18x gross and 4.15x net at Q3 2026 and USD 8,080 million of gross debt [CP-1]; this leaves limited tolerance for a downturn. Fleet capital intensity is heavy (Documentary Fact): EBITDA after net rental capex of USD 1,075 million, 7.52x gross debt, and negative Q3 2026 free cash flow of USD 69 million with USD 252 million of fleet purchases unpaid [CP-1]; this slows repayment and increases revolver use. Liquidity depends on one facility (Documentary Fact): ABL availability of USD 2,034 million is borrowing-base dependent and the AR Facility is fully drawn [CP-1]. Interest burden and floating-rate exposure (Documentary Fact): cash interest of USD 530 million over the LTM, cover of 3.65x and floating debt of USD 3,244 million [CP-1]; this exposes cash flow to short-term rates and the company says it is reevaluating its approach to floating-rate debt [CP-1A operating model], but no hedging program is described. Balance sheet quality (Documentary Fact): goodwill and intangible assets exceed equity, leaving tangible equity of negative USD 2,434 million [CP-1]; asset coverage rests on the fleet rather than on book equity. Structural position of the unsecured notes (Analyst Interpretation): USD 4,750 million of Senior Notes are unsecured and effectively junior to the secured ABL, term loan and AR Facility (USD 3,244 million drawn) to the extent of the value of collateral, and the ABL permits future pari passu or subordinated secured debt [CP-1 debt by instrument; CP-1A transaction summary]; no priming action is documented. Unverified management claims (Management Language): synergies tracking to plan and the 3.90x pro forma leverage, neither testable from the pack.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence to a cautious reading is management's own pro forma net leverage of 3.90x against 4.15x calculated here, and the improving trend (5.38x at FY2025 to 4.15x at Q3 2026). The LTM window to Q3 2026 starts after the H&E closing, so the stated pro forma element should add little, and the gap is likely add-backs (Analyst Interpretation, unverified). If the Q4 2025 release confirmed add-backs of that size and the synergy plan were quantified, the leverage view would improve. The opposite case is a downturn with a sequence the filings let us trace: construction or project demand slows and interest rates stay high; dollar utilization and rental rates soften first while fixed overhead stays; EBITDA falls against a debt balance that has barely moved; fleet purchases can be cut but used-fleet disposal proceeds depend on the resale market; free cash flow, already negative in Q3 2026, goes further negative and the ABL borrowing base shrinks with fleet values; liquidity then depends on the revolver while the AR Facility (due August 31, 2027) needs extension. Observable triggers: quarterly free cash flow, dollar utilization, ABL availability against the unquantified fixed charge trigger, and the AR Facility extension. No stress number is asserted.
